label: VALID_STEP

step: Activity and transfer: whose DNA it is cannot become what anyone did / S2
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: scope_widening; null doing positive work; category folded that the premises distinguish

(1) Quantifier: P4 characterises 'every ATF statement NAMING ROBINSON' and 'the FBI statements ABOUT HIM'; the conclusion ranges over 'the DNA results in this record' — every DNA result, including items and contributors that never name Robinson, exclusions, and any result no premise describes. step: Activity and transfer: whose DNA it is cannot become what anyone did / S3
label: INVALID_STEP

The conclusion specifies that mechanism as 'a route by which DNA can reach an item OTHER THAN through the named person's own act with that item.' Derivation from the listed premises only: P1 + P2 yield exactly 'the FBI analyst described a transfer mechanism, and she did so during the State's own examination' — i.e. a transfer mechanism of unspecified type is described in the testimony, and its presence there is not attributable to cross-examination. step: Activity and transfer: whose DNA it is cannot become what anyone did / S4
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: unsupported conjunct; scope note named but not discharged; generalization from two instances

Every restatement quoted is locational/source: 'DNA on the trigger' (P1) and 'found all over that gun... the scope, the grips, the stock, and even the trigger' (P3). None of these asserts what anyone DID: not that Robinson pulled the trigger, fired, carried, or handled the weapon at any time. Worse, P4 is an explicit scope note running the other way — the divergence is 'in ONE direction: toward source attribution' — and the step lets the conclusion range past the limitation that premise names. Naming the direction does not discharge the widening. If the argument rests on 'even the trigger' implying firing, that is an implicature, not an asserted proposition, and it is not in any premise. Secondary widenings: 'Public and charging-layer RESTATEMENTS' generalises a class from exactly two instances (a charging document and one argument by the State), with no premise about media or other public restatement; and 'the laboratory results do not carry' rests on P3's DEFENCE characterisation of what the analysts said plus §8.1's own prior judgment (P4) — the file's earlier verdict used as evidence for its present one.

Derivation from the listed premises only: P2 shows the charging phrase 'DNA on the trigger' (P1) localises to a spot within a swab the analyst could not localise within, drawn from a 4-to-7-contributor degraded mixture; P3 shows the State's 'found all over that gun' asserting presence where the analysts offered evidentiary support for inclusion as a possible contributor; P4 records the divergence as running toward source attribution. Together they support: 'the charging document's locational phrasing and the State's argument assert source- and location-level propositions stronger than the analysts' stated inclusion language.' That is narrower than the stated conclusion by exactly one conjunct — action — and by the class 'public restatements.' Narrower derivation ⇒ INVALID_STEP. Repair: drop 'and about action' (or cite a restatement that actually asserts an act), and name the two instances rather than a class.

step: Activity and transfer: whose DNA it is cannot become what anyone did / S5
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: overgeneralization to a universal modal maxim; composition assumed
gap: The first clause ('the volume of forensic material naming Robinson does not establish what he did') is within the premises. The clause after the dash is not: 'whose DNA it is CANNOT become what ANYONE did' replaces a case-scoped finding with a universal impossibility claim — quantified over any person and any DNA, and modalised to 'cannot.' Every premise is indexed to this record: 'on this record' (P2), 'each of THOSE items' (P3), 'the forensic evidence naming Robinson' (P4). Nothing licenses a general principle about what source-level results can never do; as stated it would also deny that source-level results plus transfer-and-persistence data can ever bear on activity-level propositions, which no premise asserts and which would contradict S3's own reliance on a transfer mechanism being evidentially relevant. Secondary: on a distributive reading of P1 (each result is source-level), the move from 'each item carries only source-level information' to 'their volume establishes nothing about what he did' assumes composition — that the distribution and pattern across fifteen items adds no inference the single items lack. That assumption may be defensible but is unstated. P4 is also the file's own prior judgment ('substantial in volume and narrow in what it can bear') cited as support for restating it.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: that accumulating source-level results cannot convert into an activity-level conclusion. Derivation from the listed premises only: P2 counts thirteen ATF likelihood ratios plus two FBI figures naming Robinson; P3 says each carries the same activity/timing limitation; P1 says the results carry source-level propositions only; P4 records the file's characterisation of the body of evidence. These support: 'on this record, the fifteen Robinson-naming figures, however numerous, establish source-level propositions only and do not establish what Robinson did.' That is case-scoped and person-scoped. The stated conclusion adds a general maxim about anyone's DNA and any act, and a necessity operator. Derivation narrower than stated conclusion ⇒ INVALID_STEP. Repair: keep the first clause and either drop the maxim or restate it as a case finding ('on this record, whose DNA it is has not become what anyone did').

A value that is a subjective determination by a human is by that description not a quantity an instrument measures, so the negative half of the conclusion is carried, not added. My derivation matches the stated conclusion in both scope and strength. Minor, non-fatal note: the premises speak of 'interpretation software' and the conclusion contrasts with 'the instrument' — the contrast class shifts vocabulary, but P1 and P3 independently exclude instrumental measurement of the count, so the shift does no unearned work. P3 is a '§ says' premise, but it is corroborative here; P1 and P2 carry the step without it.

step: The contributor count is an analyst input, not a measurement, and it is entangled with the same assumption / S2
label: VALID_STEP

From the premises alone I derive: the count on item 7 moved from three to two (P1); the P8 rebuild records that amendment as SUPPORTED and ties the 1.7-octillion ratio to it (P2); §8.3 records the item as a two-contributor profile (P3), so the count in force behind the reported figure is the post-amendment two. Small slack, not enough to invalidate: P1 is passive ('the count moved') while the conclusion attributes the values to 'the examiner' — the attribution is supplied by §8.3's record of the examiner's profile rather than asserted outright.

step: The contributor count is an analyst input, not a measurement, and it is entangled with the same assumption / S3
label: INVALID_STEP
gap: The premises establish conditioning at the STATISTIC stage and assumption at the IDENTITY stage; the conclusion is about the COUNT. P1 and P4 show the examiner assumed Twiggs was present because he was submitted as an elimination sample, and that she used him as an elimination in calculating Robinson's figure. P2 shows both hypotheses place Twiggs among exactly two contributors. Together these establish that WHO one of the two contributors is was supplied by assumption — they do not establish that the NUMBER two was reached by that assumption. The unstated bridging premise needed is: assuming a known individual is present constrains or fixes the number of contributors called. Nothing listed supplies it, and the competing route is left open without warrant — that the two-person call was read off the profile data (the same §8.3 material this document elsewhere cites: full profile, 5%/95% proportions) and the elimination assumption applied afterwards at the statistic stage. The only premise that closes the gap is P3, and P3 is reported, not demonstrated: it states that §8.4 finding 2 SAYS the two-person call is not independent of the elimination donor's introduction. Taken as given, P3 makes it true that the section says this; it does not make the said thing true. Using the file's own prior finding as the load-bearing link for the file's current inference is the self-certification pattern. Secondary: 'not independent of' (symmetric entanglement) becomes 'rests on' (directional dependence of the count upon the assumption); the premise does not fix the direction.
regeneration: Step tries to establish: the item-7 contributor count is founded on the same elimination assumption the conditioning problem identifies. From the premises alone I derive only: (i) the examiner's stated practice is to assume presence for an elimination-submitted individual, and she did so here; (ii) the reported ratios compare hypotheses that both seat Twiggs among exactly two contributors, so the statistic does not test his presence; (iii) §8.4 finding 2 asserts the two-person call is not independent of the elimination donor's introduction. What that supports: 'the reported statistic is conditioned on Twiggs's presence inside a two-contributor framing, and the file has found the count not independent of that introduction.' That is narrower than the stated conclusion in two ways — it reports the non-independence finding rather than establishing it, and it does not establish directional dependence of the count on the assumption. Narrower derivation than stated conclusion, therefore INVALID_STEP.
failure_type: self-certification (file's own finding as the load-bearing link) + directional strengthening ('not independent of' → 'rests on') + unbridged shift from identity/statistic to count

step: The contributor count is an analyst input, not a measurement, and it is entangled with the same assumption / S4
label: INVALID_STEP
gap: The first clause is carried; the second is not. From P1 and P2, a value that is not independent of the elimination assumption cannot serve as an independent check on it — that much is entailed. But 'so the two limitations compound rather than offsetting each other' does two unlicensed things. (a) False dichotomy: the premises support only 'do not offset' / 'share a common source.' They leave open, and the sentence forecloses without warrant, the reading that this is ONE limitation surfacing at two points — the same assumption re-described — in which case nothing aggravates anything. (b) Magnitude claim from premises that carry no magnitude: 'compound' asserts that the joint defect is worse than either alone, a statement about the size or direction of an effect. No listed premise quantifies or directs any effect; P3 is itself a null ('the statistic never tests whether Twiggs is present'), and a null cannot generate a positive claim about aggravation. Note also the tension with the sibling premise set at S5, which states the record is silent on the direction and size of any effect the assumption had — a document cannot be silent on direction and size and simultaneously know the two limitations compound. From the premises alone I derive: the count is an analyst-supplied input (P1) that is not independent of the elimination assumption (P2), therefore it cannot function as an independent test of that assumption; and the statistic itself does not test Twiggs's presence (P3), so neither element tests the assumption. label: INVALID_STEP

Narrower derivation, therefore INVALID_STEP.

gap: (1) Scope widening: premises 1 and 3 are about THIS DOCUMENT ('this document's forensic and procedural sections', '§2.1 records'), premise 2 about 'its' holdings. The conclusion ranges over 'the library.' One file's section balance does not establish the holdings balance of the corpus that contains it. (2) 'a defendant in a capital case' — no premise states that this case is capital, or that capital posture bears on documentation density. The intuition being 'run against' is imported whole. (3) 'the best-documented figure in the file' is comparative, and no premise says anything about how any other figure is documented; without a comparator the contrast cannot be evaluated. (4) Term shift: premise 1 grants that the forensic and procedural material — much of it about Robinson — is detailed and extensive, which makes him arguably the MOST documented figure; the conclusion switches 'documented' to 'documented as a person' mid-sentence, so the asymmetry it reports is between two senses of the same word rather than between the record and an intuition. Note too that premise 3's own list (residence, bedroom attribution, occupation, daily routine, parents' town, vehicle) is not nothing 'as a person'; 'barely at all' overreads it.
regeneration: Trying to establish: a headline asymmetry about how the library knows the defendant. Derivable: within this one document, the forensic and procedural sections are extensive while §2.1's established-biography list is short and confined to identity, location, a hedged occupation, routine, family town, vehicle and booking data. That supports 'in this file, Robinson is documented mainly through forensics and procedure.' It does not reach the library, does not establish a capital-case premise, and cannot rank him against other figures.

step: S5 — From the nature of the search space to "no session has ever gone looking"
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: causal leap from a null; alternatives foreclosed without warrant; document self-report used as established fact
gap: (1) The conclusion is causal — 'missing BECAUSE nobody searched' — and needs the counterfactual that searching WOULD have found the material. Premise 2 supplies the opposite kind of fact: a court-record-built library 'would not necessarily contain' biographical material, which explains why absence is unsurprising, not what caused it. Failure to search is at most a sufficient explanation among others; the premises foreclose none of the live alternatives: the material may not exist in accessible form, may be sealed or juvenile-restricted, may be paywalled, or may have been encountered and not banked. (2) Premise 3 is 'the document states that no session has ever gone looking.' Taken as given, it establishes what the document says, and the step promotes that self-report to an established fact about the project's entire search history without any independent act — no session-log or acquisition-log premise is offered. A file's own account of what it never did is the same class of evidence the project's own rules treat as needing a verification act. (3) Premise 1 leaves 'the search space' ambiguous between the corpus and the world; the conclusion needs it to mean the project's effort, which premise 1 does not say.
regeneration: Trying to establish: the cause of the biographical absence is the project's failure to search. Derivable: the library was built outward from the court record; such a library need not contain biographical material; and the document asserts that no session sought Robinson's biography or his out-of-record online presence. That supports 'the absence is consistent with, and unsurprising given, a court-record-built corpus, and the document reports no session having looked.' It does not support a causal 'because,' and it does not establish the search history as fact.

step: S6 — From "nobody looked" to "the absence is an artifact of acquisition priorities"
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: circular premise (the conclusion asserted as premise 3); term shift (effort direction → priorities); self-certification of the finding's honesty
gap: (1) Premise 3 IS the conclusion, complete with its own 'therefore' and its own foreclosure ('rather than by anything about Robinson or about what exists'). A step whose premise set contains its conclusion establishes nothing; the inferential work the step claims to do has been moved into the premises, so the exclusion of the two rival explanations is asserted, never derived. Premises 1 and 2 alone give only: nobody searched, and holdings track where effort went — which is consistent with the material also not existing, or existing only behind access the project never had. (2) Term shift: premise 2 says 'where the project DIRECTED ITS ACQUISITION EFFORT'; the conclusion says 'this project's acquisition PRIORITIES.' Effort can be directed by access, cost, docket timing, or accident; 'priorities' imputes deliberate ranking, which no premise supplies. (3) 'and saying so is the honest form of the finding' is a normative self-assessment with no premise behind it — the finding certifying its own framing as honest. The project's own rule bars a file certifying itself.
regeneration: Trying to establish: the absence is an artifact of acquisition priorities, and that framing is the honest one. Derivable from premises 1 and 2 without the question-begging premise 3: the library's holdings reflect where acquisition effort went, and no effort went to Robinson's biography — therefore the absence is CONSISTENT WITH an effort-allocation explanation. Not derivable: that effort allocation is the explanation to the exclusion of non-existence or inaccessibility; that allocation amounted to 'priorities'; or that this phrasing is the honest one.

step: S7 — The scope disclaimer: from a holdings claim to "not evidence of absence"
label: VALID_STEP
gap: No entailment gap. Premises 1–3 stipulate the finding's content (a holdings claim, not a world claim, not a claim about Robinson's facts); premises 4–5 supply the rule and the matching fact that block the absence-of-evidence inference: the rule licenses 'evidence of absence' only where the search space would necessarily contain the record, and premise 5 states this search space would not. The conclusion restates exactly that and no more. Two observations that do NOT change the verdict, because premises are taken as given: the step is near-tautological — premises 1–3 are the conclusion in other words, so the step's force is entirely the author's declaration of what the finding claims, and it therefore certifies nothing about whether the finding AS WRITTEN elsewhere stays inside that scope. In particular, this disclaimer ranges over 'the sparsity finding' only; it does not reach the causal claim in S5 or the priorities claim in S6, and a scope note here does not discharge a scope breach there.
regeneration: Trying to establish: the sparsity finding is a scoped holdings null, not evidence of absence, not a statement about Robinson. Derived from the premises alone: the finding reports this library's holdings after the described searches (premise 1); it makes no existence claim about the world and no truth claim about Robinson (premises 2–3); and under the project's own rule, a null in a search space that need not contain the record is not evidence of absence (premises 4–5). The derivation matches the stated conclusion in scope and strength — neither narrower nor wider.

step: 'Possible ridge detail and/or smudging' is not a print result / S1 — Locate what the phrase is attached to
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: exhaustiveness assumed / false dichotomy; referent granted by premise
gap: The premises license only the positive limb. 'X is a DNA swab item in Exhibit 30's calculation table' does not entail 'X is not a latent-print item' — nothing given makes the two categories mutually exclusive, and one sub-area of a rifle (trigger, bolt, barrel, optic) can be both processed for latents and swabbed for DNA; that is routine, sequence-sensitive practice. The exclusive clause 'not to latent-print items' requires an exhaustive, non-overlapping item taxonomy that no premise supplies. Secondary (premise_suspect): P2 asserts by fiat the very cross-document identification the step's title says it is performing — 'those four numbers ARE DNA swab items' grants that the ATF sub-item series and Exhibit 30's table numbering share a referent, rather than showing it. A number in one document matching a number in another is a claim someone typed, not a demonstrated identity.

Using only P1+P2 I derive: the phrase appears on four sub-items that also appear as DNA swab items carrying likelihood ratios in Exhibit 30's table. My derivation is narrower than the stated conclusion, which adds the exclusion 'not to latent-print items'. Narrower → INVALID_STEP.

step: 'Possible ridge detail and/or smudging' is not a print result / S2 — From where it sits to what kind of statement it is
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: non sequitur from position to authorship; false dichotomy on hedged wording
gap: Two unwarranted moves. (i) Position to discipline: that a note sits on an item that appears in a DNA table does not entail the note was written by, or about, the DNA-collection process. P1 places the note; it does not attribute or date it, and an evidence sheet can carry notes from more than one examination of the same item. (ii) Hedge to non-result: 'possible' and 'and/or' mark an inconclusive finding at least as readily as a siting descriptor — an inconclusive latent-print observation is worded in exactly this register, so possibility-language cannot discriminate between the two. The premise set also foregrounds the hedging while setting aside the phrase's own nouns: 'ridge detail' and 'smudging' are print-examination vocabulary describing the condition of an impression, not properties of a swab site. The unstated assumptions needed are: (a) notes appearing on DNA swab items describe only swab siting, and (b) examination results are never expressed in possibility language. Neither is given.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: the phrase's kind — siting descriptor, not fingerprint result. Using only the two premises I derive: a hedged note of unstated authorship and unstated timing appears on items that were swabbed for DNA. Its discipline of origin is undetermined; 'swab-siting note' and 'inconclusive print observation' both remain live. The stated conclusion selects one of two open options and negates the other. Narrower → INVALID_STEP.

step: 'Possible ridge detail and/or smudging' is not a print result / S3 — The meaning assignment ('it means only')
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: null doing positive work; smuggled identity; dropped disjunct
gap: Three gaps. (i) The null does positive work: 'nothing further about what was seen is stated anywhere on this record' bounds what the record says, not what the phrase means. From record silence it follows that the record states no more — not that the phrase 'carries no content beyond' the given reading. Unstated content is precisely what silence leaves open. (ii) Observer identity is imported: the conclusion says 'a person who swabbed saw'; no premise makes the observer and the swabber the same person, nor fixes the observation to the moment of swabbing. (iii) A disjunct is dropped: the phrase is 'possible ridge detail AND/OR smudging', and the paraphrase keeps only 'something that might have been ridge detail', silently discarding the smudging limb — an observation about the condition of an impression, not about where a swab was taken. Premise-suspect: P2 is a record-wide universal null ('anywhere on this record') offered as a bare given, with no search scope, query terms or access-path caveat attached; per this project's own standard a null is a claim needing a verification act with a stated scope, and this one arrives pre-repaired.

Using only P1+P2 I derive: on this record, the only stated content is that the phrase is a siting descriptor, and no further explication appears anywhere. That supports 'the record states nothing more about what was seen' — not 'the phrase carries nothing more' — and it identifies no observer. Narrower → INVALID_STEP.

step: 'Possible ridge detail and/or smudging' is not a print result / S4 — The un-asked question, used as support
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: inference from absence of a question to absence of an answer; scope widening (witnesses → record)
gap: The premise constrains one channel; the conclusion quantifies over the whole record. A competing on-record interpretation can arise without anyone being asked: testimony volunteered rather than elicited, the report's own legend or definitional text, an appended lab protocol, a stipulation, counsel's colloquy or argument, or other testimony describing how the rifle was processed. The unstated assumption needed is that interpretations enter the record only as answers to questions put to witnesses — an exhaustiveness assumption about how records are made. Note also the direction of work: even a true 'no rival on the record' finding is a null, and a null does not confer support on the S3 reading; it only removes one class of contradiction.

Using only the premise I derive: no witness was asked to interpret the phrase, therefore no interpretation was elicited by examination question. Whether the record contains an interpretation arriving by any other route is untouched. Narrower → INVALID_STEP.

label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: record statement treated as world fact; referent shift in 'what was swabbed'
gap: Two moves. (i) Listing to fact: the premise is what Exhibit 30's disposition column *lists*; the conclusion asserts the material *no longer exists*. That requires the unstated assumption that the disposition entries are accurate and current as of the writing date. The premise names its documentary scope and the conclusion drops it — naming a scope does not discharge it. (ii) Referent shift: the grammatical object of 'what was swabbed' is the location — trigger and trigger guard, bolt, barrel, optical accessory — and those surfaces sit on a rifle that is itself in evidence; consumption of collected swab material does not entail that the annotated location cannot be re-examined. 'Cannot be re-examined' also ranges wider than 'the swab is consumed': extracts, electropherograms, bench notes and photographs are re-examinable artifacts the premise says nothing about. If this limb is meant to support 'nothing about these four annotations can now be checked', it does not reach that.

Using only the premise I derive: Exhibit 30's disposition column lists 1.4, 1.6 and 1.9 as entirely consumed and 1.3 as retained — i.e. the swab material for three items is *recorded* as consumed. step: 'Possible ridge detail and/or smudging' is not a print result / S6 — What the chain is for: protecting §8.5's opening null
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: term shift (result vs. examination); keyword-search null not in contact with the disputed entry
gap: The premise meant to defuse the defeater and the null it defends are about different objects. P3 denies the phrase is a fingerprint *result*; §8.5's null (P1) asserts that no latent-print *examination* appears anywhere in the record. A note recording that someone looked at a rifle surface and saw what might be ridge detail or smudging can be an appearance of a print-relevant examination while not itself being a result — so the term shifts between the step's two ends. Discharging the null would need the stronger, unsupplied premise: 'the phrase neither is nor evidences any latent-print examination.' Secondary: P1 grounds the null in a text search of 35,743 lines returning zero *rifle latent* hits. A keyword null is scoped to its query terms, and the entry at issue is precisely one that a 'rifle latent' query would not return — so the null's stated basis and the disputed entry never come into contact, and P2 concedes the print reading is available to a reader. Naming the search scope in the premise does not discharge it. Structurally, the non-contradiction rests on the chain's own reading (S2), which was itself secured partly by the absence of any competing on-record reading (S4): the null and the reading protecting it are mutually supporting rather than independently established.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: that the annotation is not a counterexample to §8.5's null. Using only P1–P3 I derive: the phrase is not a fingerprint result, so it is not a latent-print *result* appearing on the record. Whether it is an appearance of a latent-print *examination* — what the null actually denies — is settled by no premise. Narrower → INVALID_STEP.

label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: exhaustiveness_assumed + term_shift (consumption → consumption-and-retention) + scope_widening (page 8 → Exhibit 30 → all ATF items)
gap: Three distinct gaps. (1) 'Taken to page 8' fixes what the witness was SHOWN, not the extent of what he testified about. Nothing in the premises forecloses his testimony ranging past that page, or a later page/exhibit covering the 15.x/18.x series; the step needs the unstated assumption 'a witness directed to a page testifies only to the items printed on it.' (2) The exhaustiveness premise is about CONSUMPTION only — 'the only other consumption testimony anywhere in the record is the FBI examiner's' — while the conclusion quantifies over 'all consumption AND RETENTION testimony.' Retention testimony by any other witness is nowhere foreclosed; the term widens between premise and conclusion. (3) P2 excludes 15.x/18.x from page 8 alone. The conclusion requires them to be outside Exhibit 30 entirely (it says all such testimony 'concerns either Exhibit 30's items or FBI items, and none of it reaches 15.1/18.1'), and no premise places them outside Exhibit 30.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: that no consumption-or-retention testimony anywhere on the record touches ATF 15.1/18.1. From the three premises alone I can derive only: while on page 8 of Ex. 30 the ATF DNA section chief's testimony concerned the 1.x–5.x items, and the only other body of CONSUMPTION testimony is the FBI examiner's about FBI items. That supports at most 'no page-8-anchored consumption testimony reaches 15.1/18.1.' Strictly narrower than the stated conclusion on two axes (retention testimony; testimony by that same witness away from page 8), so INVALID_STEP.

step: S2 — The searches
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: null_doing_positive_work (absence of a string treated as absence of a proposition) + unclosed scope in a re-run premise that states an act, not a result
gap: The premises report STRING searches; the conclusion is about PROPOSITIONS. To carry, it needs the unstated (and false-on-its-face) assumption that any passage stating consumption status must contain the stem 'consum' AND that any reference to these items must contain the literal strings '15.1'/'18.1'. 'Used up', 'exhausted', 'nothing remained', 'preserved', 'retained', 'we still have the extract' all state consumption status without 'consum'; 'item fifteen point one', '15-1', '15.1.1', 'Q15.1', or a purely descriptive reference all evade the numeral search. Second gap: the two searches are over different files — 'consum' in day4.txt only, the item numbers in day5.txt only. The cross terms are never reported ('15.1' in day4, 'consum' in day5), yet the conclusion ranges over all banked transcripts. P3 names a wider re-run but states only that the act occurred on 2026-09-14 — no terms, no result. A premise that names a broader scope does not thereby discharge it.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: propositional silence across the banked transcripts. From the premises I derive only: the stem 'consum' is absent from day4.txt under both U+FFFE readings; the strings '15.1' and '18.1' are absent from day5.txt; and some re-run occurred on 2026-09-14. That supports 'these specific strings do not occur in these specific files' — not 'no passage states whether the items were consumed or retained.' Narrower, so INVALID_STEP.

step: S3 — From the two nulls to record-silence
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: scope_widening (testimony ∪ banked transcripts → 'this record')
gap: Both premises are bounded to two containers: bodies of TESTIMONY (P1) and the BANKED TRANSCRIPTS searched (P2). The conclusion ranges over 'this record,' which in a preliminary-hearing posture also contains the admitted documentary exhibits themselves — Ex. 30 and, decisively here, Ex. 33, the very document from which 15.1 and 18.1 come — plus lab reports, stipulations, filings, and any transcript portion not banked. A DNA report can state on its face that an extract was consumed with no witness ever being asked about it. Nothing in the premises forecloses that, and the step needs the unstated assumption 'the record = testimony + banked transcripts.'
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: the status is nowhere on the record. Using only P1 and P2 I derive: no body of testimony and no banked-transcript passage addresses the consumption status of 15.1/18.1. That is a null over two named containers, not over the record. Narrower than the stated conclusion ('not on this record at all'), so INVALID_STEP — and this is the sentence the whole disposition rests on.

step: S4 — The disposition rule
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: unbounded prohibition (record-relative premise → unrestricted norm) + missing deontic premise
gap: P1 is explicitly record-relative ('not stated ON THIS RECORD'); the conclusion's 'may not be written as retained' is unrestricted, foreclosing the possibility that a source outside this record (the ATF lab report, a stipulation, later testimony) establishes retention and licenses writing it. Separately, both premises are descriptive and the conclusion is deontic ('must be written', 'may not be written'). The bridging norm — only what the record establishes may be asserted as fact — is a real project rule but is not among the listed premises, so the premises alone cannot carry the 'must'/'may not'. Substantively the disposition is right; as an entailment from these two premises it is not closed.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: an unconditional writing rule. From the premises I derive: this record does not establish retention, and 'not stated' is not interchangeable with 'retained,' so retention may not be asserted ON THE STRENGTH OF THIS RECORD. Narrower than the stated conclusion by the scope qualifier, so INVALID_STEP at low severity — the fix is one clause ('on this record'), not a rewrite.

step: S5 — The scope consequence for the consumption count
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: scope_widening within the corrective itself (ratio-bearing subset of Ex. 30 → Exhibit 30)
gap: P1 counts the ELEVEN RATIO-BEARING items in State's Exhibit 30 — six consumed, five retained, disjoint, none unaccounted. No premise says Exhibit 30 contains only ratio-bearing items, and the surrounding material (page 8 alone carrying the 1.x through 5.x series) makes it likely it does not. So the count's true denominator is 'the ratio-bearing items in Ex. 30,' not 'Exhibit 30.' The conclusion's positive half names a wider scope than the premises establish — the same class of scope error the step exists to correct, one level down. The negative half ('may not be written as a count over ATF items generally') does follow a fortiori.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: the correct scope label for the 6-of-11 count. From the premises I derive: the count is over the eleven RATIO-BEARING items of Ex. 30, and may not be written over the thirteen ratio-bearing ATF items across the record, nor over ATF items generally, because two of the thirteen are unaccounted. My derivation is narrower than 'scoped to State's Exhibit 30,' so INVALID_STEP — repairable by writing the denominator out in full.

step: S6 — Register disposition
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: self_certification (the file's own label offered as warrant for that label) + scope_widening to 'downstream' with no premise reaching there + idle premise
gap: (1) 'Downstream' is unreached. No premise says anything about other documents; the taint-propagation rule that would carry the prohibition into DNA-E01 or any citing file is a protocol rule, not a listed premise, and P3 merely cites a location ('the analytic home is cited as DNA-E01 §6.2') without doing any inferential work — it is idle, and citing a home is not governing what that home may write. (2) P2 is this document's own §16 sink entry, offered as a premise for the disposition it is supposed to justify. What makes UNVERIFIED the right label is 'the page-8 and Day-4 reasoning' it rests on, not the existence of the entry; using the entry as warrant is a judgment licensing itself. (3) The conclusion is conjunctive and its first conjunct is trivial — 'is labeled unverified' follows from P2 by restatement — so the step's whole burden falls on the second conjunct, which the premises do not carry.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: an unrestricted, this-file-and-beyond prohibition on using the proposition as fact. From the premises I derive: this document labels the proposition UNVERIFIED, and by that label's own governing column it may not appear as fact in this document's main text. Nothing about any other file follows. Narrower than 'anywhere in this document or downstream,' so INVALID_STEP.
premise_suspect_note: P2 is the file's own register entry supplied as evidence for the correctness of that entry; it also imports the contested page-8 / Day-4 reasoning by reference rather than stating it.

step: Finding 6 / S1
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: scope widening + a null doing positive work + unstated empirical generalization
gap: The premises are entirely about what the FORENSIC RECORD contains (LRs, 'aligned' language, no source attribution). The conclusion is about what THE PUBLIC will characteristically do with it. Nothing in the premises links record content to audience behaviour. The missing premise is the empirical generalization 'lay/public readers characteristically restate likelihood ratios as source attributions' — a claim about people, not about this record, and it is nowhere stated. Two further unwarranted moves: (a) 'the characteristic error' is a superlative/exhaustiveness claim — the premises foreclose no competing candidate error (e.g. treating 'aligned' as identification, treating a partial mixture as a single donor, misreading the LR magnitude), so nothing licenses singling out one as THE error; (b) 'predictable in advance' asserts a forecast, whereas the premises support at most 'if such an error occurs, it is identifiable as this type.' The null (premise 3: no analyst attributed DNA to Robinson) is doing positive work here — an absence of source attributions in the record is being converted into a positive prediction about an error to come.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: that the transposed conditional is the expected, predictable public error about this record. What the premises actually support: 'Every statement about Robinson in this record is a likelihood-ratio/inclusion statement and none is a source attribution; therefore ANY restatement of this record as a source attribution would be an instance of the transposed conditional, and would be identifiable as such.' That is a conditional identification rule, not a prediction, and not a uniqueness claim. My derivation is strictly narrower than the stated conclusion on two axes (prediction, and 'the characteristic' error), so the step overreaches.

step: Finding 6 / S2
label: VALID_STEP
gap: No material gap. The conclusion is a strict re-description of the quoted premise, and it narrows rather than widens: 'all over that gun' is dropped, and only the enumerated parts are carried forward. Two implicit identifications are carried — 'the defendant' = Robinson, and 'that gun' = the rifle — and neither is stated in the premise; in a case-specific proceeding, the referent of 'the defendant' is warranted, and the gun/rifle substitution introduces no content the enumerated parts (scope, grips, stock, trigger) do not already carry. Noted, not charged as a defect. Note also that the conclusion is correctly framed at the level of ATTRIBUTION ('a party stated'), not adoption — it claims only that the words were spoken, which is exactly what the premise gives.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: that a party said, on the record, that Robinson's DNA was on named rifle parts. What the premise supports: the State argued in the record that the defendant's DNA was on the scope, grips, stock and trigger. Derivation and stated conclusion match in scope (the derivation is if anything slightly wider than the conclusion, since the premise also contains 'all over that gun'). No overreach.

step: Finding 6 / S3
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: party characterisation promoted to established content + term shift ('conditional') + alternative foreclosed without warrant
gap: Three distinct gaps. (1) Premise 2, taken as given exactly as stated, gives only that THE DEFENCE ASSERTED what the analysts said. The conclusion treats that assertion as the analysts' actual words ('converted a ... statement into ...'), which requires the unstated premise that the defence's characterisation is accurate. One party's account of a third party's report is not the third party's report; the defence is an interested party in exactly the way the State is. (2) Term shift: 'evidentiary support for the inclusion of Tyler Robinson as a possible contributor' is an inclusion/support statement. Calling it 'a conditional' — i.e. a probability conditioned on a hypothesis, the thing a transposed conditional transposes — imports the LR characterisation from elsewhere (S1's §9 premise), which is not among THIS step's premises. Without it, the 'transposed conditional' label cannot attach: what these two premises show is a gap between 'possible contributor' and 'was found', which is a source-attribution overclaim, not necessarily the specific probabilistic inversion named. (3) 'Converted' forecloses, without warrant, that the State was characterising something else — other testimony, the ATF statements, cumulative evidence — rather than restating this particular analyst statement. The premises establish no derivational link from the analysts' wording to the State's sentence, only that both exist and conflict.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: that the State's argument is an on-record instance of the transposed conditional. What the premises actually support: 'The State's argument asserted the DNA was found on the rifle's parts; the defence asserted the analysts had said only that there was evidentiary support for Robinson's inclusion as a possible contributor; the two characterisations are inconsistent, and if the defence's account is accurate the State's assertion is stronger than the analysts' wording.' That is a disputed overstatement contingent on one party's account — narrower than an established conversion, and narrower still than the named fallacy. The step overreaches.

step: Finding 6 / S4
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: presupposition smuggled into the conclusion (the error) + a correction treated as proof of the thing corrected + unsupported 'in argument' / 'on the record'
gap: Judged standalone, as instructed, the single premise contains no error at all — it contains a defence statement. The conclusion's definite article, 'THE error', presupposes an established error that this premise does not supply and that I am forbidden to import from S3. A party stating a correction is not evidence that the thing corrected was wrong: the defence's answer establishes a dispute, not a defect. Second, the conclusion adds two location claims the premise does not carry: 'in argument' (the premise says only 'in the same proceeding' and 'in answer to the State's characterisation' — it never says the characterisation occurred in argument rather than, say, examination or a filing) and 'on the record' (from 'in the same proceeding', which is a venue, not a record status). Only 'was contested there' is close to earned, and even it is earned as 'the characterisation was contested', not 'the error was contested'.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: that the error was made in argument, on the record, and contested there. What the premise supports: 'The defence, in the same proceeding, offered a competing account of the analysts' statement in answer to the State's characterisation' — i.e. the characterisation was disputed within the proceeding. step: Finding 6 / S5
label: INVALID_STEP
failure_type: term shift on who the constraint binds + self-certification (witness's own confirmation as compliance) + 'downstream' asserting a derivational link the premises do not supply
gap: (1) The governing gap is the addressee of the norm. FBI/DOJ reporting limits bind the examiner and the laboratory's reporting; prosecuting counsel making a closing or argumentative characterisation is not a party to those reporting standards. 'The reporting constraint ... was broken' therefore shifts 'constraint' from a rule the examiner is subject to into a general prohibition on anyone in the courtroom restating the evidence. The premises license 'the State's characterisation is inconsistent with what those limits would permit in a report'; they do not license that the constraint itself was violated, because the State was never inside its scope. (2) 'Held at the examiner level' rests solely on the examiner's own confirmation. Take the premise as given and what is given is that she CONFIRMED compliance; that her confirmation is accurate is an unstated further assumption — a witness certifying her own conformity is the self-certification pattern, not an independent finding. (3) 'Downstream of her testimony' asserts a chain: that the State's argument descends from, restates, or is derived from her testimony. The premises give only temporal order ('later'). The State may have been characterising ATF statements, other testimony, or nothing in particular. Temporal succession is not downstream-ness. Note also 'the reporting constraint' (singular) standing in for four distinct limits, none of which is stated — nothing tells us the State's sentence conflicts with all four, or with any specified one.
regeneration: What the step tries to establish: that a constraint intact at the examiner level was broken further down the chain. What the premises support: 'Four reporting limits were put to the examiner and she testified she had followed them; the State's argument later characterised the evidence as a source attribution — a characterisation that would not have been permissible under examiner-level reporting limits had the examiner made it.' That is a contrast between a witness's claimed compliance and a lawyer's later words, not a breach of the constraint, and not a causal chain. Narrower on all three terms; the step overreaches.

step: Finding 6 / S6
label: INVALID_STEP

gap: (1) Premise 3 — that the P7 verdict was 'recorded as NARROWED rather than killed' — is the project's own bookkeeping about its own judgment, offered as evidence that its judgment stands. A prior recorded disposition cannot be evidence that the current disposition is sound; that is exactly the self-certification pattern the protocol names. A finding survives on premises, never on the label its last review round was filed under. (2) Premise 2 establishes that the two quoted passages EXIST. label: INVALID_STEP
